days.title: Secret Entrance
days.approach: Parses lines into signed rotations (L negative, R positive); part 2 replaces each value n with `replicate (abs n) (sgn n)`. Each list gets 50 prepended, a mod-100 running sum via `scanl1`, and a `counts` lookup of 0.
days.critique: `⥢` duplicates the parsed list and `⇲` maps the expansion over only the second copy, so one `both` pipeline serves both parts. Part 2 materialises every unit step, so its work grows with the summed rotation magnitudes. `counts` builds a frequency Map of all visited positions just to read key 0; `|!` returns a bare value, so missing-key behaviour depends on quaalude.
days.html: module Day1 (part1, part2) where ((part1, part2) :: (ℤ', ℤ')) = ($(aoc 1) |-.. ((*) <$> (((string "L") $> (-1)) <|> ((string "R") $> 1)) <*> number)) ⥢ (⇲ (>>= ((replicate $@) . (abs &&& sgn)))) & both ((50 :) >>> scanl1 ((`mod` 100) .<. (+)) >>> counts >>> (|! 0))

days.title: Gift Shop
days.approach: Parses comma-separated ranges and enumerates every integer in each. Digit count comes from logBase; an ID matches if repeating its leading l/s digits s times rebuilds it, and matches are summed via `Σ`.
days.critique: The check is arithmetic with no string conversion. Part 2 passes [1 .. 10], and with s = 1 the check reduces to i == i, so every positive ID matches and the filter does nothing; starting the list at 2 avoids this. It is also brute force, floating-point logBase can miscount near powers of ten, and repetition counts above 10 are never tested.
days.html: module Day2 (part1, part2) where invalid :: ℤ -> ℤ -> ℤ -> Bool invalid i l s = let t = l `div` s r = i `div` (10 ^ (l - t)) o = sum [r * 10 ^ j | j <- [0, t .. l - 1]] in t * s == l && i == o aRange :: [ℤ] -> Parser (Σ ℤ) aRange s = do (a, b) <- (,) <$> (number <* char '-') <*> number let o = [Σ i | i <- [a .. b], let l = floor (logBase 10 (fromInteger i)) + 1, any (invalid i l) s] pure (o <>!) part1 :: Σ ℤ part1 = $(aoc 2) |-<> csvOf (aRange [2]) part2 :: Σ ℤ part2 = $(aoc 2) |-<> csvOf (aRange [1 .. 10])

days.title: Lobby
days.approach: For each digit line, a recursion over (index, digits remaining) either skips or takes the current digit and keeps the larger e-digit value; line results are summed for e=2 and e=12.
days.critique: One function covers both parts through the digit count, and Maybe marks suffixes too short to fill the remaining digits. Recursive calls go through .$. into an MM monad keyed on the Ord (index, remaining) pair, so cost depends on that prelude machinery. The nested Maybe cases are wordy, and the quaalude operators (.$., ?, |-<..>) are hard to read without knowing the prelude.
days.html: module Day3 (part1, part2) where j :: Integer -> Vector ℕ₁₀ -> ℤ j e bs = let n = size bs go :: (ℤ, ℤ) .->. Maybe ℤ go (i, e) | e == 0 = pure (Just 0) | i == n = pure Nothing | otherwise = do aM <- go .$. (i + 1, e) bM <- go .$. (i + 1, e - 1) case bM of Nothing -> pure aM Just b' -> let b = b' + (fromIntegral (bs !! i) * 10 ^ (e - 1)) in case aM of Nothing -> pure . Just $ b Just a -> pure . Just $ max a b in (? 0) . run $ go .$. (0, e) (part1 :: ℤ, part2 :: ℤ) = both (\e -> $(aoc 3) |-<..> (Σ . j e . co <$> many nat₁₀)) (2, 12)

days.title: Printing Department
days.approach: Each round finds every '@' cell with fewer than four '@' among its eight neighbours, removes them together through grid updates, and adds up the counts. Part 1 runs one round; part 2 runs until no cell qualifies.
days.critique: One `remove` with a round limit covers both parts. Passing -1 never hits the 0 case, so recursion ends only when `removable` returns empty. Every round rescans the whole grid instead of rechecking only the neighbours of removed cells. Candidates go into a set of Maybe-wrapped coordinates, which is then queried with `Just c` for each coordinate. A plain filter would be more direct.
days.html: module Day4 (part1, part2) where removable :: ".@" ▦ ℤ² -> [ℤ²] removable g = let cs = g & unGrid & fmap ( \(c, x) -> if x == (#"@" □) && size [n | n <- neighs @8 @[] c g, g |! n == (#"@" □)] < 4 then Just c else Nothing ) & mkSet in [c | c <- coords g, Just c ∈ cs] remove :: ℤ -> ".@" ▦ ℤ² -> ℤ remove 0 _ = 0 remove n g = case removable g of [] -> 0 cs -> size cs + remove (n - 1) (foldl' (\g c -> g |. (c, (#"." □))) g cs) g :: ".@" ▦ ℤ² = $(grid 4) (part1, part2) :: ℤ² = (remove 1 g, remove (-1) g)

days.title: Cafeteria
days.approach: Template Haskell embeds and parses the input into ranges and IDs. Part 1 counts IDs that fall in any range. Part 2 applies `Ŀ` with a combinator to the sorted ranges and measures the result with `|.|`.
days.critique: Part 1 filters the IDs with `or` over per-range `∈` tests, costing O(ids × ranges); merging the ranges and binary-searching would avoid the full scan. Part 2 combines `(<<*>>) ∘ (max <:>)` and `(⇱) ∘ (-!) ∘ (|.|)` via `&.&` and passes this to `Ŀ` over `(fst i) 🎜`. `Ŀ` has no given signature, so how this combination behaves on the ranges cannot be determined from the code shown, and the dense point-free style makes it hard to follow.
days.html: module Day5 (part1, part2) where i :: ([RangeOf ℤ] ≠ []) × ([ℤ] ≠ []) = ($(aoc 5) ⋯) part1 :: ℤ = ((snd i |-?-> (or ∘ (<$> fst i) ∘ (∈))) |.|) part2 :: ℤ = (((Ŀ (((<<*>>) ∘ (max <:>)) &.& ((⇱) ∘ (-!) ∘ (|.|))) ((fst i) 🎜)) !>) |.|)

days.title: Trash Compactor
days.approach: Parses the input into number groups `ps` and operator functions `ops`. For part 2, it splits raw lines, applies `(⊤)`, cuts at all-space rows, filters digits and parses each group.
days.critique: `both` runs one shared pipeline on `ps` and `psᵀ`: zip with `ops`, apply `Ŀ` via `$@`, then `!>`, then `Σ`, and combine with `<>!`. So the parts differ only in how the numbers are grouped. `<$$>` keeps the nested group structure through filtering and parsing. Readability suffers from dense, unsigned quaalude operators such as `Ŀ`, which make the core per-problem combining step opaque.
days.html: module Day6 (part1, part2) where (ps, ops) :: [[ℕ]] × [ℕ -> ℕ -> ℕ] = (⊤) . un ⇱ ($(aoc 6) |- (⋮×⋯)) psᵀ :: [[ℕ]] = ((splitOn "\n" $(aoc 6)) ⊤) & splitBy (all (== ' ')) & ((isDigit <-?-|) <$$>) & ((⋯) <$$>) (part1, part2) :: (Σ ℕ, Σ ℕ) = both ((<>!) . ((Σ . (!>) . (Ŀ $@)) <$>) . (zip ops)) (ps, psᵀ)

days.title: Laboratories
days.approach: Parses a grid of 'S', '^' and '.' cells and binds the single 'S' position. A recursive function steps along increasing y from it, branching diagonally at '^' and returning a position set plus a count.
days.critique: One traversal yields both answers: part 1 is the size of the returned set, part 2 the count, which adds 1 at each off-grid exit. Recursive calls go through .$. into an MM value unwrapped by run, and every '^' unions two child sets. The dense operator style is hard to read, and the refutable [s] pattern fails unless there is exactly one 'S'.
days.html: module Day7 (part1, part2) where (g, [s]) :: ("S^." ▦ ℤ², [ℤ²]) = ($(aoc 7) ⋯) ⥢ (⇲ (|?> (#S □))) go :: ℤ² .->. (Set ℤ², ℤ) go (x, y) = ((⊏⊐) <$> g |? (x, y) ? ' ') ?> ((== ' ') ->> pure ((∅), 1)) : ( (== '^') ->> do (a, b) <- go .$. (x - 1, y + 1) (c, d) <- go .$. (x + 1, y + 1) pure ((x, y) |-> a ∪ c, b + d) ) : ((∈ ['S', '.']) ->> go .$. (x, y + 1)) : [] (part1, part2) :: ℤ × ℤ = (|.|) ⇱ run (go s)

days.title: Playground
days.approach: Sorts all box pairs by squared distance and merges circuits held as a Set of Sets. Part 1 applies `Ł connect` over the first 1000 pairs, then multiplies the three largest sizes. Part 2 merges until one circuit remains.
days.critique: Sorting pairs once by integer squared distance (`ssd³`) avoids floating point, and that sorted list drives both parts. Each `connect` filters the circuit set twice with `(<-?-|)` to find the two endpoints' circuits, where union-find would avoid repeated searches. `final` has no empty-list case, so it is partial. The 1000 and `take 3` in `part1` are literal constants.
days.html: module Day8 (part1, part2) where boxes :: [ℤ³] = (($(aoc 8) |- parseVia @([CSV ℤ 3] ≠ [])) ⊏) ps :: [ℤ³ × ℤ³] = sortOn (ssd³ $@) (triPairs boxes) circuits :: Set (Set ℤ³) = mk (mk . pure <$> boxes) connect :: Set (Set ℤ³) -> ℤ³ × ℤ³ -> Set (Set ℤ³) connect c (a, b) = let (aC, bC) = both (head' . (<-?-| c) . (∈)) (a, b) c' = aC ∪ bC |-> c |\ aC |\ bC in aC == bC ??? c $ c' final :: Set (Set ℤ³) -> [ℤ³ × ℤ³] -> (ℤ³, ℤ³) final circuits (p : ps) = let circuits' = connect circuits p in (circuits' |.|) == 1 ??? p $ final circuits' ps part1 :: Π ℤ = ((Π <$> take 3 ((((Ł connect circuits (take 1000 ps) !>) ⊏) <&> (|.|)) 🎝)) <>!) part2 :: ℤ = (*) $@ both fst3 (final circuits ps)

days.title: Movie Theater
days.approach: Parses input with `(⋮)` at type `[ℤ ⹉ 2] ≠ []`, builds `out` via `outside ∘ loopPairs` and `rects` via `triPairs`, then runs one `|-?->`, `ds²`, `🎝`, `Ȟ`, `!>` pipeline per predicate.
days.critique: `<:>` applies one shared pipeline to a pair of predicates, `(⊨)` for part 1 and `not ∘ or ∘ (out <&>) ∘ (□?□)` for part 2, so the parts differ only in that predicate. In part 2 every pair produced by `triPairs` is tested with `□?□` against every element of `out`, a brute-force pairs-times-edges scan. The geometry lives in unshown helpers such as `outside` and `□?□`.
days.html: module Day9 (part1, part2) where (part1, part2) :: ℤ × ℤ = let (out, rects) = (((⋮) @([ℤ ⹉ 2] ≠ []) $(aoc 9)) ⊏) & outside ∘ loopPairs &&& triPairs in ((!>) ∘ Ȟ ∘ (🎝) ∘ (ds² <$@>) ∘ (rects |-?->)) <:> ((⊨), not ∘ or ∘ (out <&>) ∘ (□?□))

days.title: Factory
days.approach: Part 1 runs a breadth-first search over string states starting from all '.', toggling characters per button, with a Set of seen states. Part 2 encodes press counts as Z3 integer variables and minimises their sum under per-counter equality constraints.
days.critique: The BFS is direct but explores up to 2^n states and enqueues every successor before checking whether it was already seen, so the Seq queue grows larger than needed. Part 2 hands the integer program to Z3, which keeps it short but leaves the method opaque. Machines with no solution are silently dropped by (<>?) rather than reported.
days.html: module Day10 where xs :: [(𝕊, [[ℤ]], [ℤ])] = $(aoc 10) & (⋮⊏) @( [ TupSep " " ( (Between "[" "]" (𝕊 ⭀ ".#")), [Between "(" ")" (CSVAny ℤ)], (Between "{" "}" (CSVAny ℤ)) ) ] ≠ [] ) part1 :: ℤ = let tog '#' = '.' tog '.' = '#' press ls bs bi = ((Ł (\ls li -> ls !. (li, tog (ls !! li))) ls (bs !! bi)) !>) go' (ls', bs, _) = let lsE = const '.' <$> ls' go seen ((n, ls) :<| q) | ls == ls' = n | ls ∈ seen = go seen q | otherwise = go (ls |-> seen) (foldl' (\q bi -> q |> (n + 1, press ls bs bi)) q (range 0 ((bs |.|) - 1))) in go ((∅) @(Set 𝕊)) (mk₁ (0, lsE)) in sum (go' <$> xs) part2 :: ℤ = let go :: [[ℤ]] -> [ℤ] -> Maybe (ℤ, [ℤ]) go bs js' = z3 $ minimize "n_min" do ns <- sequence [z3IntVar ("n" <> show i) | (i, _) <- enum bs] n <- z3Add ns js <- traverse z3Int js' preds <- sequence [ (forM ns (\n -> z3Ge n =<< z3Int 0)), (forM (enum js) (\(ji, j) -> z3Eq j =<< z3Add [n | (n, b) <- zip ns bs, ji ∈ b])) ] z3Assert =<< z3And (preds <>!) pure (n, ns) in sum $ sum <$> ([snd <$> (go bs js) | (_, bs, js) <- xs] <>?)

days.title: Reactor
days.approach: Parses the input into a map from node names to successor lists and counts paths by recursion; part 2 recurses over (sawDac, sawFft, node) states through the `.$.` helper, unwrapped with `run`.
days.critique: Carrying two flags in the state lets one recursion count only paths that visit both `dac` and `fft`. Part 1 is plain recursion with no visible caching, so shared suffixes are recomputed. Neither part tracks visited nodes, so a reachable cycle would not terminate. The Unicode operators and Template Haskell input splice keep the code short but opaque without the custom prelude.
days.html: module Day11 (part1, part2) where g :: 𝕊 :|-> [𝕊] = $(aoc 11) & (⋮) @(MapSep ": " (𝕊 ⭀ AaZz) [𝕊 ⭀ AaZz]) part1 :: ℤ = let go n = n == "out" ??? 1 $ sum (go <$> g |! n) in go "you" part2 :: ℤ = let go (dac, fft, "out") = pure (dac && fft ??? 1 $ 0) go (dac, fft, n) = sum <$> sequence [go .$. (dac || (n == "dac"), fft || (n == "fft"), n') | n' <- g |! n] in run $ go (False, False, "svr")

days.title: Christmas Tree Farm
days.approach: part1 counts regions where the summed cell counts of the requested presents (count times shape size) is at most w·h; part1' instead runs a priority-queue search over placements of rotated and flipped shapes.
days.critique: part1 is a single area comparison per region, linear in input size, and does not try to place any shape. part1' enumerates shape orientations with uniq and prunes states whose remaining required area exceeds free cells. Its ordering key and nested sections are very dense and hard to follow without knowing quaalude.
days.html: module Day12 where part1' :: ℤ part1' = let (ps, rs) :: [(ℤ, ".#" ▦ ℤ²)] × [(ℤ², [ℤ])] = ($(aoc 12) & (⊏|⊐) @(([(ℤ, ".#" ▦ ℤ²) ⯻ ":\n"] ≠ []) × ([(ℤ² ⯻ "x", [ℤ] ⯻ " ") ⯻ ": "] ≠ []))) vs :: [[Set ℤ²]] = uniq ∘ (((⌞) ∘) <$> ((∘) <$> [id, (↻), ((↻)) ∘ ((↻)), ((↺))] <*> [id, ((◓)), ((◐))]) <*>) ∘ φ ∘ ͼ ∘ (|?> (#"#" □)) ∘ snd <$> ps go Φ = False go ((((w, h), ns), ((x, y), s)) :<!! q) = all (≡ 0) ns ∨ (ⵉ ((((|.|) ∘ (⟒)) <$> vs, ns) ⤊ (⋅)) |≤| s) ∧ (go (((\((_, ns), (_, s)) -> (ⵉ (ns <&> (^ 2)), -(s |.|))), [(((w, h), ns'), (x ∈ (0 ⥅ w - 3) ??? (x + 1, y) $ (0, y + 1), s')) | (ns', s') <- (ns, s) : [(ns !. (i, n - 1), s ∖ v) | (i, n) <- (ns ..#), n > 0, v <- vs !! i <&> (⇆⇅ (x, y)), v ∩ s ≡ v]]) ||-> q)) ∨ go q in rs |?| (go ∘ mkℤ₁ ∘ (⇲ (((0, 0),) ∘ box₀ @Set ∘ fst)) ∘ dup) part1 = let (ps, rs) :: [(ℤ, ".#" ▦ ℤ²)] × [(ℤ², [ℤ])] = $(aoc 12) & (⊏|⊐) @(([(ℤ, ".#" ▦ ℤ²) ⯻ ":\n"] ≠ []) × ([(ℤ² ⯻ "x", [ℤ] ⯻ " ") ⯻ ": "] ≠ [])) in rs |?| \((w, h), ns) -> ⵉ [n ⋅ (ͽ p |.|) | ((_, p), n) <- ps ⇑ ns] ≤ w ⋅ h
